title: Top 275 PDF: Words 201 to 225
subtitle: Puckish to Vicissitude (SSC CGL 2026 Digital Notes)

words.meaning: Playfully mischievous, especially in a fun or harmless way.
words.example: The mischievous child played a harmless prank on his friends.

words.meaning: Thin, supple, and graceful in movement.
words.example: The gymnast was admired for her lissome and effortless routines.

words.hindi: छोटी बात में कमी निकालने वाला / तुनकमिज़ाज
words.meaning: Placing too much emphasis on trivial or minor details; fussy.
words.example: The editor was pernickety about punctuation and formatting.

words.meaning: Swollen, enlarged, or affectedly pompous.
words.example: Heavy monsoon rains left the mountain river tumid and fast-flowing.

words.meaning: Of or occurring every day; daily and ordinary.
words.example: Reading the morning newspaper is part of his quotidian routine.

words.hindi: संक्रामक / एक से दूसरे में फैलने वाला
words.meaning: Relating to fermentation or infectious, contagious diseases.
words.example: Clean drinking water helps prevent zymotic illnesses.

words.meaning: Green with grass or other rich vegetation.
words.example: After the monsoon, the entire valley turned verdant.

words.hindi: हवा की नमी से घुलने वाला
words.meaning: Becoming liquid, or having a tendency to melt or dissolve by absorbing moisture from the air.
words.example: Certain salts are deliquescent and must be stored in airtight jars.

words.meaning: Relating to or given to eating; devouring or voracious.
words.example: Growing teenagers often have an edacious appetite.

words.meaning: Shining brightly; dazzling.
words.example: The fulgent sun rose above the snow-covered peaks.

words.meaning: Having or encouraging an excessive interest in sexual matters; indecent.
words.example: The censor board removed the prurient scenes from the film.

words.meaning: Overly theatrical or melodramatic in character or style.
words.example: He made a histrionic display of grief to gain sympathy.

words.meaning: Soon passing out of sight, memory, or existence; quickly fading.
words.example: A rainbow is a beautiful but evanescent phenomenon.

words.meaning: Containing little moisture; very dry.
words.example: Cacti are well adapted to survive in xeric environments.

words.hindi: कड़वाहट और गुस्से से भरा / कटु
words.meaning: Angry and bitter in speech or debate.
words.example: The property dispute led to an acrimonious argument.

words.meaning: Make false and defamatory statements about someone.
words.example: False rumours were used to calumniate the honest officer.

words.hindi: किसी को नीचा दिखाना / बदनाम करना
words.meaning: Criticize unfairly; disparage or belittle.
words.example: True sportsmanship means you never denigrate your opponent.

words.meaning: Feel or express great loathing for; detest intensely.
words.example: Peace-loving citizens execrate all forms of violence.

words.meaning: Of doubtful authenticity, although widely circulated as being true.
words.example: Most stories about the haunted fort are purely apocryphal.

words.meaning: Naturally accompanying or associated with something.
words.example: Hard work and its concomitant success go hand in hand.

words.meaning: Intended to teach, particularly in having moral instruction as an ulterior motive.
words.example: Panchatantra stories are entertaining as well as didactic.

words.meaning: Conceal one's true motives, feelings, or beliefs.
words.example: An honest witness does not try to dissemble the facts.

words.meaning: Extremely idealistic; unrealistic and impractical.
words.example: Expecting to master vocabulary in a single day is a quixotic idea.

words.meaning: Refusing to submit to an authority or to comply with a regulation.
words.example: Strict action was taken against the recusant members.

words.meaning: A change of circumstances or fortune, typically one that is unwelcome.
words.example: True friends stand by you through all the vicissitudes of life.
